extracted.intended_audience: science educators and education researchers (K-12 teachers, teacher educators, curriculum designers)
extracted.subtask_description: An exploratory evaluation of ChatGPT's outputs about science pedagogy, including how it can generate units, rubrics, quizzes, and be used as a research tool; identifies pedagogical quality criteria and ethical/disclosure considerations for educators. Focuses on designing classroom resources (Year 7 example) and reflective use in research.

rubrics_metrics.name: Active and inquiry-based learning
rubrics_metrics.description: Effective science teaching encourages students to actively engage in the learning process through hands-on activities, experiments, and inquiry-based projects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This approach allows students to make connections between what they are learning and the world around them; underpins many example learning experiences in the ChatGPT output and aligns with research emphasising student engagement with inquiry, ideas, and evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Real-world connections
rubrics_metrics.description: Effective science teaching makes connections between what students are learning in the classroom and real-world applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Connecting curriculum to students' lives increases relevance and engagement (e.g., using videos/pictures of community energy challenges). ChatGPT's output and Hackling & Prain both stress this as important.

rubrics_metrics.name: Differentiation
rubrics_metrics.description: Effective science teaching takes into account the diverse needs and learning styles of students, using a variety of strategies to differentiate instruction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include providing multiple ways to access information, varied assessment methods, simplified guiding questions or extra time for students who struggle, and scaffolding templates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collaboration
rubrics_metrics.description: Effective science teaching fosters a collaborative learning environment where students work together to solve problems and share ideas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collaboration helps develop communication, problem-solving, and teamwork skills; the 5Es unit example uses group research and group proposals as concrete tasks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of technology
rubrics_metrics.description: Effective science teaching incorporates technology to enhance student learning via simulations, virtual labs, online resources, and other digital tools.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ICT should be 'exploited to enhance the learning of science with opportunities to interpret and construct multimodal representations' (Hackling & Prain). Consider access and equity when choosing tech tools.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessment (varied methods)
rubrics_metrics.description: Effective science teaching uses a variety of assessment methods to measure student understanding and provide feedback to guide instruction, including formative, summative, and performance-based assessments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The ChatGPT output recommends formative and summative assessments and performance tasks; assessment should facilitate learning and focus on outcomes that contribute to scientific literacy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Professional development
rubrics_metrics.description: Effective science teaching requires ongoing professional development for teachers to stay current with the latest research, best practices and new technologies in the field of science education.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ChatGPT listed professional development as a characteristic; while some seminal lists omit it, the paper notes PD helps teachers interpret and adapt AI-generated resources appropriately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Students experience a curriculum relevant to their lives and interests (Hackling & Prain)
rubrics_metrics.description: Curriculum should be relevant to students' lives and interests (Hackling & Prain element).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Relevance increases engagement and supports connections to broader community and students' prior knowledge.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classroom science linked with the broader community (Hackling & Prain)
rubrics_metrics.description: Science classroom activities should be linked to the broader community.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: community-focused problems (e.g., local energy challenges) that situate learning in sociocultural context; ChatGPT's output less explicitly emphasised this, so educators may need to adapt AI suggestions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Students actively engaged with inquiry, ideas, and evidence (Hackling & Prain)
rubrics_metrics.description: Students should be actively engaged with inquiry, ideas, and evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This reinforces inquiry-based learning and the need for students to work with evidence rather than passively receive information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Students are challenged to develop and extend meaningful conceptual understandings (Hackling & Prain)
rubrics_metrics.description: Instruction should challenge students to develop and extend meaningful conceptual understandings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tasks should push students beyond surface knowledge to deeper conceptual reasoning; the Year 7 unit asks capable students to design sustainable energy plans to promote deeper thinking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessment facilitates learning and focuses on outcomes that contribute to scientific literacy (Hackling & Prain)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment should facilitate learning and focus on outcomes that contribute to scientific literacy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assessment design should support learning goals and measure meaningful outcomes (not just rote recall). Use rubrics and performance assessments aligned to literacy goals.

rubrics_metrics.name: ICT exploited to enhance learning with multimodal representations (Hackling & Prain)
rubrics_metrics.description: Information and communication technologies should be used to enhance learning and create opportunities for multimodal representations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourage students to interpret and construct multimodal artifacts (visuals, simulations); ensure technology use aligns with pedagogy and accessibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: 5Es model implementation (Engage, Explore, Explain, Elaborate, Evaluate)
rubrics_metrics.description: Design units using the 5Es model: Engage (pose real-world problem), Explore (group research), Explain (present/interpret findings), Elaborate (create/apply solutions), Evaluate (self/peer/teacher assessment).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The ChatGPT-generated Year 7 unit provides concrete examples for each phase (video of community issue, guided group research, presentations with visual aids, proposal creation with criteria, rubrics and debates). Educators should refine generic suggestions to context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rubric categories and level scales (ChatGPT example)
rubrics_metrics.description: Self-assessment rubric categories identified by ChatGPT include understanding, research, participation, each with a four-level scale: exemplary, proficient, developing, emerging.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The ChatGPT rubric is a useful starting point but described as 'too vague to identify specific indicators' — educators are advised to add specific, observable indicators for each level and adapt formatting for ease of copying into Word.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quiz design with answer key
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment items (e.g., multiple-choice quizzes) should test conceptual understanding and include an answer key.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ChatGPT generated Year 7 multiple-choice questions and an answer key; teachers should check for accuracy and clarity and adapt distractors and stems to match learning goals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide scaffolding and support for struggling students
rubrics_metrics.description: Units and tasks should include supports for students who struggle (simplified guiding questions, extra time, graphic organisers, templates, sample proposals, step-by-step guides).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ChatGPT's unit repeatedly suggests providing additional scaffolding during Explore/Explain/Elaborate phases; scaffolding should be concrete and tailored to learner needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance teacher-centred and student-centred pedagogies
rubrics_metrics.description: Effective practice may require balancing direct instruction ('chalk and talk') and student-centred approaches (inquiry, project-based learning).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ChatGPT recommends a balance and using a variety of teaching methods (hands-on activities, group work, discussions) while the paper questions where the evidence for a 'balance' lies and emphasises context sensitivity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposal design criteria for extended tasks
rubrics_metrics.description: When asking students to design proposals (e.g., sustainable energy plan), specify criteria such as cost-effectiveness, environmental impact, and reliability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Providing explicit criteria guides student work and assessment; ChatGPT's unit example lists these as mandatory plan requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessment practices including self-assessment, peer-assessment, and teacher feedback
rubrics_metrics.description: Include self-assessment (students check rubric levels), peer-assessment of presentations/plans, and teacher feedback/grading.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The unit example uses rubrics for student self-assessment and peer review, complemented by teacher feedback; combine methods to promote reflection and formative feedback.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence grounding and citation accuracy
rubrics_metrics.description: Educational resources and claims should be grounded in evidence and supported by accurate references.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The paper warns ChatGPT 'continually provides false and misleading references' and may mix correct and non-existent citations. Educators must verify sources and avoid treating AI output as authoritative without checking evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contextual sensitivity (recognise local/student/context factors)
rubrics_metrics.description: Pedagogical recommendations must consider context (individual student needs, school profile/priorities, curriculum, access to resources).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The author repeatedly notes that ChatGPT output is generic and must be adapted to local contexts; context determines appropriateness of pedagogy and assessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bias, representation, and voice (algorithmic skew)
rubrics_metrics.description: AI-generated content can perpetuate harmful biases and is often skewed toward Western perspectives, potentially silencing other voices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OpenAI acknowledges bias risks; educators should interrogate whose perspectives are reflected and explicitly teach critical evaluation of sources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethical considerations of AI use
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider environmental impacts of large models, labor and content-moderation harms (e.g., low-paid workers exposed to disturbing material), and copyright infringement risks when using or assigning AI-generated material.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The paper suggests discussing these ethical matters with students, modelling responsible use, and considering broader implications beyond classroom convenience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency and disclosure when using LLMs in research
rubrics_metrics.description: Journals (e.g., Nature/Springer Nature) require that large language models are not listed as accredited authors and that researchers disclose use of LLMs in methods or acknowledgements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disclosure practices may evolve; researchers should follow journal policies, and treat LLM assistance analogously to other tools (but explicitly disclose where it affected the work).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of ChatGPT as a research tool (editing, rewriting, summarising)
rubrics_metrics.description: ChatGPT can assist researchers with editing prose, rewriting sentences, organising thinking, generating feedback, writing code, and summarising literature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The author reports mixed results—some sentences improved, others were better pre-editing. Use LLMs experimentally, verify outputs, and reflect on changes; maintain transparency about the tool's role.
